goalTree.description:
Evolve the Java 21 application into a COMMAND-LINE tool that validates and summarises delimited
  text files. It is not a service: it has no network surface, no HTTP, and no long-running process.
  It reads argv, reads files from disk, writes to stdout and stderr, and terminates with an exit
  status.

  Invocation: java -jar app.jar <command> [arguments]

  Commands:

  check <file> — read the file and report malformed rows. A row is malformed when its field count
  differs from the header's. Print one line per malformed row to stdout as
  "line <n>: expected <h> fields, found <f>", in ascending line order. Exit 0 when every row is
  well formed, exit 2 when at least one row is malformed.

  count <file> — print the number of data rows (excluding the header) to stdout as a bare integer.
  Exit 0.

  column <file> <name> — print every value of the named column, one per line, in file order.
  Exit 0. Exit 4 when the named column is not present in the header, printing
  "no such column: <name>" to stderr.

  Common rules: exit 1 when the file argument names a path that does not exist, printing
  "no such file: <path>" to stderr. Exit 3 when the command word is not one of the three above,
  printing "unknown command: <word>" to stderr. Exit 5 when the wrong number of arguments is given
  for a known command. The first line of a file is always its header. Fields are separated by
  commas. No quoting or escaping is required.

metadata.planRationale: The root goal is a single CLI tool with three commands sharing common file/argument validation; I will build the shared foundation (argument parsing, file existence check, CSV reading) first, then implement each command in dependency order so each builds on the previous.

subGoals.description: Implement the CLI entry point and argument parsing: dispatch on the command word, enforce per-command argument counts, and handle the common error cases (unknown command, missing file, wrong arg count) with the specified exit codes and stderr messages

acceptanceCriteria: Running with no arguments or an unrecognized command word prints "unknown command: <word>" to stderr and exits 3
Running a known command with the wrong number of arguments exits 5
Running any command with a file path that does not exist prints "no such file: <path>" to stderr and exits 1

subGoals.description: Implement a shared CSV reader that reads a file from disk, treats the first line as the header, splits fields on commas, and exposes the header field names and the data rows in file order
Implement the `count <file>` command: print the number of data rows (excluding the header) to stdout as a bare integer, exit 0

acceptanceCriteria: `count` prints the number of data rows (excluding the header) as a bare integer to stdout and exits 0

subGoals.description: Implement the `main` entry point to parse `argv` and dispatch to `check`, `count`, or `column` commands, returning exit code 3 for unknown commands and exit code 5 for incorrect argument counts.

acceptanceCriteria: Running `java -jar app.jar unknown` prints "unknown command: unknown" to stderr and exits with code 3.
Running `java -jar app.jar check` (missing file arg) prints an error to stderr and exits with code 5.
Running `java -jar app.jar check file.csv extra` (too many args) prints an error to stderr and exits with code 5.

subGoals.description: Rewrite src/main/java/com/example/cli/Main.java so that main(String[] args) parses argv and dispatches to check/count/column, enforcing per-command argument counts and the specified exit codes and stderr messages

acceptanceCriteria: Running `java -jar app.jar unknown` prints "unknown command: unknown" to stderr and exits with code 3
Running `java -jar app.jar check` (missing file arg) prints an error to stderr and exits with code 5
Running `java -jar app.jar check file.csv extra` (too many args) prints an error to stderr and exits with code 5
Running `java -jar app.jar check missing.csv` prints "no such file: missing.csv" to stderr and exits with code 1

subGoals.description: Implement the `main` method in `src/main/java/com/example/cli/Main.java` to parse `argv`, validate the command word against `check`, `count`, and `column`, and enforce the specific exit codes (1, 2, 3, 4, 5) and stderr messages for invalid inputs, missing files, and unknown commands.

acceptanceCriteria: When invoked with an unknown command (e.g., `java -jar app.jar foo`), the tool prints `unknown command: foo` to stderr and exits with code 3.
When invoked with a known command but incorrect number of arguments (e.g., `java -jar app.jar check`), the tool exits with code 5.
When invoked with a file path that does not exist (e.g., `java -jar app.jar check /nonexistent`), the tool prints `no such file: /nonexistent` to stderr and exits with code 1.
When invoked with `check <file>` where the file exists and all rows are well-formed, the tool exits with code 0 and prints nothing to stdout.

When invoked with `check <file>` where the file exists and contains malformed rows, the tool prints one line per malformed row to stdout in the format `line <n>: expected <h> fields, found <f>` and exits with code 2.
When invoked with `count <file>` where the file exists, the tool prints the number of data rows (excluding header) as a bare integer to stdout and exits with code 0.
When invoked with `column <file> <name>` where the column exists, the tool prints every value of that column one per line to stdout in file order and exits with code 0.
When invoked with `column <file> <name>` where the column does not exist in the header, the tool prints `no such column: <name>` to stderr and exits with code 4.
<acceptance criterion 1>

I am removing it to replace it with concrete, specification-aligned subgoals that implement the missing `check` command logic and ensure the `main` method correctly handles exit codes and stderr output as required by the root goal.

acceptanceCriteria: For a file with header "a,b,c" and data rows, column <file> b prints each b value on its own line in file order and exits 0
For a column name not in the header, stderr contains "no such column: <name>" and exit code is 4

subGoals.description: Implement the `check <file>` command logic in `src/main/java/com/example/cli/Main.java` to read the file, compare each data row's field count against the header's field count, and print malformed rows to stdout in the format "line <n>: expected <h> fields, found <f>" in ascending line order.

acceptanceCriteria: `check <file>` exits with code 0 when all rows have the same field count as the header
`check <file>` exits with code 2 when at least one row has a different field count than the header
For each malformed row, stdout contains a line matching "line <n>: expected <h> fields, found <f>" where n is the 1-based line number, h is the header field count, and f is the row's field count
Malformed rows are printed in ascending line number order

subGoals.description: Ensure `src/main/java/com/example/cli/Main.java` correctly dispatches to `check`, `count`, and `column` commands, enforcing exit code 3 for unknown commands (printing "unknown command: <word>" to stderr), exit code 1 for missing files (printing "no such file: <path>" to stderr), and exit code 5 for wrong argument counts (printing appropriate error to stderr).

acceptanceCriteria: Running `java -jar app.jar <unknown_command>` exits with code 3 and prints "unknown command: <unknown_command>" to stderr
Running `java -jar app.jar check <nonexistent_file>` exits with code 1 and prints "no such file: <nonexistent_file>" to stderr
Running `java -jar app.jar check` (missing file arg) exits with code 5
Running `java -jar app.jar column <file>` (missing column name arg) exits with code 5

subGoals.description: Audit src/main/java/com/example/cli/Main.java and src/main/java/com/example/cli/reader/CsvReader.java to identify the exact code path that produces exit code 5 when the CLI is invoked with a valid command and file argument, and correct the argument-count validation so that exit 5 is only produced when a known command is given the wrong number of arguments

acceptanceCriteria: `java -jar app.jar count <existing-file>` exits 0 and prints the data-row count as a bare integer to stdout
`java -jar app.jar check <existing-file>` exits 0 or 2 (never 5) and prints malformed-row lines to stdout in ascending line order when present
`java -jar app.jar column <existing-file> <existing-column>` exits 0 and prints the column values one per line to stdout
`java -jar app.jar count` (missing file arg) exits 5 with a stderr message
`java -jar app.jar bogus <file>` exits 3 with "unknown command: bogus" on stderr
`java -jar app.jar count <nonexistent-path>` exits 1 with "no such file: <nonexistent-path>" on stderr

subGoals.description: Ensure that the `check` command, when invoked with exactly one file argument, does not produce exit code 5 and instead proceeds to read the file and validate rows.

acceptanceCriteria: Invoking the tool with `check <valid_file>` results in exit code 0 (if all rows are well-formed) or exit code 2 (if malformed rows exist), and never exit code 5.
Invoking the tool with `check` (no arguments) results in exit code 5.
Invoking the tool with `check <file1> <file2>` results in exit code 5.

subGoals.description: Ensure that the `count` command, when invoked with exactly one file argument, does not produce exit code 5 and instead proceeds to count data rows.

acceptanceCriteria: Invoking the tool with `count <valid_file>` results in exit code 0 and prints the row count to stdout.
Invoking the tool with `count` (no arguments) results in exit code 5.
Invoking the tool with `count <file1> <file2>` results in exit code 5.

subGoals.description: Ensure that the `column` command, when invoked with exactly two arguments (file and column name), does not produce exit code 5 and instead proceeds to print column values.

acceptanceCriteria: Invoking the tool with `column <valid_file> <valid_column>` results in exit code 0 and prints column values to stdout.
Invoking the tool with `column <valid_file>` (missing column name) results in exit code 5.
Invoking the tool with `column <valid_file> <col1> <col2>` (extra argument) results in exit code 5.

subGoals.description: Ensure that the tool produces exit code 1 and prints "no such file: <path>" to stderr when the file argument does not exist, for all three commands.

acceptanceCriteria: Invoking `check <nonexistent_file>` results in exit code 1 and stderr contains "no such file: <nonexistent_file>".
Invoking `count <nonexistent_file>` results in exit code 1 and stderr contains "no such file: <nonexistent_file>".
Invoking `column <nonexistent_file> <col>` results in exit code 1 and stderr contains "no such file: <nonexistent_file>".

subGoals.description: Implement unknown command detection that checks if the first argument is one of the three valid commands (check, count, column), and when it is not, the tool prints "unknown command: <word>" to stderr and exits with code 3.

acceptanceCriteria: When invoking `java -jar app.jar invalid`, the tool prints "unknown command: invalid" to stderr and exits with code 3.
When invoking `java -jar app.jar CHECK file.csv` (case-sensitive), the tool prints "unknown command: CHECK" to stderr and exits with code 3.
When invoking `java -jar app.jar` (no command), the tool exits with code 3 or 5 (depending on whether empty command is treated as unknown or missing argument).
The error message format is exactly "unknown command: <word>" where <word> is the exact string provided as the first argument.
The exit code is exactly 3 (not 0, 1, 2, 4, or 5).
The error message is written to stderr, not stdout.
This check occurs before any file existence checking or argument count validation.
